Download GitHub Enterprise Server 3.21.10 November 17, 2026 📣 This is not the latest release of Enterprise Server. Please use the latest release for the latest security, performance, and bug fixes. 3.21.10: Features Administrators can use --metrics-days N with the support bundle utilities to collect metrics for a positive number of days independently of the log collection period. The --metrics-only option collects metrics, metrics-related logs, and bundle metadata without other diagnostics. By default, bundles include 10 days of metrics on standalone instances and clusters with up to 20 nodes. For larger clusters, the default decreases based on cluster size, to a minimum of three days. 3.21.10: Security fixes Packages have been updated to the latest security versions. HIGH: Updated Git to include fixes that address CVE-2026-105437 , CVE-2026-111760 , CVE-2026-113408 , CVE-2026-114466 , CVE-2026-114467 , and CVE-2026-114469 . This update was previously communicated in the release notes for the last patch release, but had not been fully resolved. HIGH: On a GitHub Enterprise Server instance in a cluster configuration, an attacker authenticated as a site administrator could execute arbitrary commands as the host git user on peer Git server nodes outside the pre-receive hook sandbox by supplying a crafted download URL for a custom pre-receive hook environment. GitHub has requested CVE ID CVE-2026-112740 for this vulnerability, which was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program . HIGH: A site administrator could modify host files with root privileges and disclose private repository data due to improper path validation in pre-receive hook environment setup. To mitigate this issue, GitHub has strengthened path validation. GitHub has requested CVE ID CVE-2026-116637 for this vulnerability, which was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program . HIGH: An organization member could read and modify another user's private repositories due to improper SSH certificate identity validation. Exploitation required an instance using built-in authentication and a valid certificate issued to the attacker by a trusted SSH certificate authority. Access was limited to repositories within that authority's scope. GitHub has requested CVE ID CVE-2026-116643 for this vulnerability, which was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program . HIGH: An authenticated attacker could read private file paths and available source-code excerpts by supplying another repository's review-thread IDs through a pull request they could access. This authorization bypass required no victim interaction. GitHub has requested CVE ID CVE-2026-111801 for this vulnerability, which was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program . HIGH: An attacker with a session for a user whose numeric ID matched an enterprise's ID could generate private keys for its GitHub Apps by bypassing ownership checks. Repository access depended on the App's installations and permissions. On standard fresh installations, the collision involved the non-loginable ghost account; the reported reproduction required site administrator impersonation. GitHub has requested CVE ID CVE-2026-110307 for this vulnerability, which was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program . HIGH : An attacker with permission to manage custom-property definitions and edit values could add an SSH key to another member's personal account through stored HTML in a single-select option. Exploitation required a definition manager in the same organization to attempt to remove the in-use option and save with a valid sudo session. GitHub has requested CVE ID CVE-2026-131800 for this vulnerability, which was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program HIGH: A user with repository write access could exploit server-side request forgery in Slack webhook validity checks, potentially leading to remote code execution on the appliance. Exploitation required Secret Protection with secret scanning and validity checks for partner patterns enabled. GitHub has requested CVE ID CVE-2026-131820 for this vulnerability, which was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program . HIGH: An OS command injection vulnerability in the GitHub Pages deployment process could allow arbitrary command execution as the GitHub Pages service user on a GitHub Enterprise Server instance. Exploitation required an authenticated user with permission to deploy a GitHub Pages site. GitHub has requested CVE ID CVE-2026-130824 for this vulnerability, which was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program . MEDIUM: A user with write access could bypass branch protections through specially crafted input when resolving pull request conflicts. GitHub has requested CVE ID CVE-2026-131647 for this vulnerability, which was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program . LOW: SAML authentication could match an incorrect account when NameID values differed only in case, accents, or trailing spaces. These mismatches now return a login-conflict error. LOW: Secret scanning validity checks for Google Cloud service account credentials were hardened to prevent HTTP redirects from sending validation requests to unintended destinations. Redirect responses leave the secret's validity as unknown. An attacker with write access to a repository with secret scanning enabled could execute arbitrary code on the instance by committing a crafted Google Cloud service account credential whose token URI pointed to an internal service on the instance. When GitHub Enterprise Server ran a validity check on the detected secret, it sent a request to the attacker-controlled URL. Validity check requests are now blocked from reaching internal services on the instance. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program . 3.21.10: Bug fixes When users cloned or fetched a repository over SSH with compression enabled, the operation could stall until the connection timed out, especially for repositories with many references. Administrators could not apply SSH cipher configurations containing only CTR ciphers because ghe-crypto and the Management Console incorrectly rejected these lists. Site administrators could not apply configuration changes when the backup CPU quota ( backup.cpu-quota ) was set to a valid percentage, such as 320% or 12.5% , because configuration validation rejected the percent sign. On instances configured with multiple trusted IP addresses or CIDR ranges for the Prometheus metrics endpoint, ghe-config-check reported validation errors for valid comma-separated lists. On instances with legacy metrics enabled, the weekly cleanup did not remove metrics files that had not been updated for more than 90 days. These stale files continued to consume space on the root disk. Site administrators could not apply configuration changes when the backup schedule ( backup.schedule ) was set to a valid cron schedule, such as 0 0 * * * , because configuration validation rejected whitespace and * . Administrators restoring backups on standalone instances could find that Redis loaded existing append-only file (AOF) data instead of the restored backup. Redis restores could also fail for backups in RDB version 11 format. Site administrators could not apply configuration after upgrading an instance with a custom OpenTelemetry pipeline that referenced the built-in otlp/ghes receiver. Site administrators whose GitHub Actions storage settings included values such as "github" saw those values incorrectly redacted from hostnames and database names in support bundles, resulting in false diagnostic failures. After OpenTelemetry metrics were disabled, collectd could stop receiving application and service metrics until it was restarted. Administrators running ghe-live-migrations could see duplicate timestamps and stray formatting characters in the output. Sending SIGTERM to the utility did not always stop the underlying migration container cleanly, and the utility did not reject some invalid options. When an administrator changed redis.io-threads and applied the configuration, Redis on the primary could restart with the previous value, so the change did not take effect. After a site administrator applied a hotpatch, some files that the hotpatch installed, such as command-line utilities, could be missing from the instance. On clusters with automatic MySQL failover enabled, upgrades could continue without successfully disabling failover, potentially causing an unexpected promotion of a MySQL replica. Upgrades stop before shutting down MySQL if failover suppression cannot be confirmed. Upgrades and other operations that drain a node could take about 10 seconds longer than necessary because an internal service did not shut down promptly when signaled. After an upgrade, ghe-config-apply verified the same Docker images more than once, unnecessarily extending the configuration run. Configured appliances reused as replicas in a high availability configuration could come online before replication started. On instances configured to forward logs over UDP, a journal message of approximately 64 KiB or larger could stop all subsequent log forwarding until syslog-ng was restarted. Site administrators could not trigger an Elasticsearch snapshot backup by setting backup.es-backup-strategy in ghe-config . On standalone or high-availability instances, repository data could be restored even when the corresponding repository metadata was missing from the database backup. Newly created repositories could then be preinitialized with that orphaned data. Administrators configuring repository caches on instances with GitHub Actions enabled saw a mssql-server and mysql-server should have the same value warning during replication setup or configuration runs. Users with qualifying issue or pull request activity did not see the "Recent activity" section on their personal dashboards. On instances with a large number of committers, enabling security features on a repository, including by applying a security configuration, could time out while calculating remaining GitHub Advanced Security licenses. This calculation is now skipped when enabling the repository uses no additional licenses. If calculating GitHub Advanced Security license usage took too long while an enterprise owner applied a security configuration, the confirmation dialog did not show how many repositories the configuration would apply to. When site administrators added or re-added a repository cache replica, repositories could remain unavailable on the cache, causing requests routed to it to return Repository not found errors until the background scheduler repaired them. Site administrators could encounter an error when viewing pending fine-grained personal access token requests associated with a deleted token. Organizations could receive email notifications about pending fine-grained personal access token requests after the associated tokens had been deleted. On instances running in private mode with subdomain isolation enabled, users could intermittently encounter broken avatar images and failures when loading content from the media, notebooks, and viewscreen subdomains. Users experienced failed Git pushes when secret scanning evaluated delegated bypass requests configured with an organization custom role. Secret scanning alerts for enterprise-level custom patterns did not include links to the custom pattern settings. For teams linked to SCIM external groups, the site administrator dashboard displayed a Sync action that called a service unavailable on GitHub Enterprise Server and a description that incorrectly indicated membership would reconcile automatically. Site administrators can use the Reconcile action to reconcile team membership. Background processes handling issue and project updates could consume increasing amounts of memory. Updates to organization rulesets targeting many repositories could time out. Users could be incorrectly classified as dormant despite recent activity, such as commenting on issues or pull requests.
